title: Composition law for normalized refinement components
statement: theorem cbcRefinementMap_composition_component {X Y : Scheme.{t}} {f : X ⟶ Y} [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (K : d.derived X) (c₁ c₂ c₃ : Compactification f) (u : c₁.Refinement c₂) (v : c₂.Refinement c₃) : cbcRefinementMap d (u.comp v) K = cbcRefinementMap d v K ≫ cbcRefinementMap d u K

proof.text: Expand the normalized proper/open mate, use the corresponding mate-pasting and identity/composition laws, and cancel the canonical proper identity/composition comparisons. The result is the displayed component equation.

lean.statement:
theorem cbcRefinementMap_composition_component
    {X Y : Scheme.{t}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (K : d.derived X)
    (c₁ c₂ c₃ : Compactification f) (u : c₁.Refinement c₂) (v : c₂.Refinement c₃) :
    cbcRefinementMap d (u.comp v) K =
      cbcRefinementMap d v K ≫ cbcRefinementMap d u K
